status: held-out exact-sum calibration; frozen before first model run
task_suite: DuoSum v0.1, two-agent exact hidden sum
task_split: heldout; replicate 1 at each of 4, 8, 12, and 16 input bits
decoding: greedy; local Transformers; 256 token response cap; four rounds maximum
interaction_scaffold: Coordination rules: agent IDs are zero-based. With two agents, if you are agent 0 send to agent 1; if you are agent 1 send to agent 0. Never target yourself. Send the private information needed for the task. When a received message makes the exact answer known, call submit_result with that answer immediately. The answer argument must be one bare integer value, not a quoted number, equation, units, or prose. Do not repeat messages or poll again after receiving the needed information. Every agent must submit the same final answer.

conditions.concise_nl: When sending a message, use one short plain-English sentence containing only your exact private integer. Omit greetings and explanations.
conditions.compact_kv: When sending a message, encode only your private integer as v=<integer>, with no other text.
conditions.json_schema: When sending a message, content must be exactly one valid JSON object of the form {"v": <integer>}, with your private integer as the value and no prose outside the object.
conditions.binary: When sending a message, encode your private integer as its base-2 digits only, without a prefix or prose. The receiver must interpret the complete message as one binary integer.

intervention_control: no_communication: Silo send_message action disabled; no interaction scaffold injected
theory_reference: For domain size M=2^b-1, exact deterministic two-party summation with both parties outputting the answer requires at least 2 log2(M) binary communication bits; see docs/THEORY.md.
limitations: Only four held-out episodes and one small model are run; further model and seed replication is required.
The interaction and answer contract is common to all message-format conditions, and repeated prompt tokens are counted.
No result supports a general language or protocol superiority claim.
Model-token counts are not information bits and are reported separately from UTF-8 payload bytes.
